wake.speaker: Shivers
wake.dialogue:
The cold comes up through the floorboards first. Then the smell — ash, spilled pastis, something older underneath.
You are lying face down in a room that has already forgotten you.

inventory-of-pain.speaker: Pain Threshold
inventory-of-pain.dialogue: *Everything catalogues itself.* Left shoulder: bruised. Ribs: negotiable. Mouth: tastes of copper wiring.

sit-up.speaker: Physical Instrument
sit-up.dialogue: Get up. Nobody is going to lift you.

room.speaker: Perception
room.dialogue: A rented room, top floor. One window, curtain half torn. A chair on its side. And there, by the radiator — a shape under a coat that is not a coat.

options.label: Look at the shape by the radiator.
Go to the window instead. Whatever it is, it can wait.

body.speaker: Visual Calculus
body.dialogue:
Angles. The chair fell east, the bottle rolled west, and the shape was moved — twice. Someone tidied, then thought better of it.

Something in the reconstruction refuses to close.

body-after.speaker: Half Light
body-after.dialogue: You do not want the arithmetic. You want the door. *Now.*

options.label: (Go through the pockets first. You will hate yourself either way.)

kneel.speaker: Empathy
kneel.dialogue:
"I don't know your name yet. I'm going to find it out."
The room does not soften, but you do, a little.

pockets.speaker: Interfacing
pockets.dialogue: Lining, seam, a folded card that tears at the corner as you pull it. Whatever was written on the missing corner was the part that mattered.

window.speaker: Shivers
window.dialogue: Below: a wet street, a tram wire humming to itself, a district that has been holding its breath for forty years. It will not tell you what happened here. It never does.

voice.speaker: Volition
voice.dialogue: Your own voice comes back at you flat and unfamiliar. Good. It means you still have one.

hallway.speaker: Composure
hallway.dialogue: The corridor is narrow and the carpet has been the same colour since before the war. Straighten your collar. Whoever is downstairs will read you in under a second.

options.label: Down the stairs. Get it over with.
(Back into the room. You left something unfinished.)

listen.speaker: Reaction Speed
listen.dialogue: A floorboard, two doors down. It settles before you can turn your head. Someone else is awake on this landing.

landing.speaker: Inland Empire
landing.dialogue: The room wants you to stay a moment longer. Rooms like this always do — they are collectors.

options.label: Go downstairs and find whoever rented you this room.
(Sit on the edge of the bed. Just for a minute.)

mirror.speaker: Electrochemistry
mirror.dialogue: Look at that face. That is the face of a man who was *magnificent* eleven hours ago and cannot prove it.

stay.speaker: Volition
stay.dialogue: A minute. Not more. You are allowed a minute and then you are going to be a person again.

stairs.speaker: Esprit de Corps
stairs.dialogue: Somewhere below, a woman is counting coins into a tin and thinking about which of her tenants she will have to lie for this week.

bar.speaker: Authority
bar.dialogue:
"Nobody leaves this building. Not until I've had a look at the top floor."
The words come out too loud and half a size too big for you.

bar-after.speaker: Suggestion
bar-after.dialogue: She has already decided what you are. There is still room to decide *which kind.*

options.label: "That came out wrong. I'm asking, not ordering."
"There is a dead man in room eleven and I don't know how I know that."
(Say nothing. Walk out into the street.)

apology.speaker: Empathy
apology.dialogue: Her shoulders come down a centimetre. That centimetre is worth more than the whole speech before it.

lie.speaker: Drama
lie.dialogue: *Sublime.* The clipboard you are not holding has never been more real.

truth.speaker: Encyclopedia
truth.dialogue:
• Room eleven has been let to the same name for six years.
  • That name is not the name you woke up with.
She goes very still, and you understand that she already knew.

exit.speaker: Hand/Eye Coordination
exit.dialogue:
The front door handle is loose in its plate. You catch it before it drops, set it back, and step out into the rain.
*Something starts here.*
